title: New ways to look
blurb: Tilted slices, two states side by side, a volume render, and a morph between states.

steps.title: Any slice, not just y = 0
body: The cross-section can tilt, turn or slide off the nucleus, and the axes say exactly which plane you are looking at.
Signed ψ is offered only where ψ is real on the plane. A complex orbital on a tilted plane shows its density instead, because dropping its imaginary part would draw half a function.

steps.title: Two states, one frame
body: A second state can sit beside the first, on the same frame and one colour scale. He⁺ has twice hydrogen's charge, so its 2p is half the size and far brighter.
Neither picture is rescaled to fill its frame, so size and brightness compare directly.

steps.title: The density as a glowing fog
body: The 3-D view can draw the whole density at once, ray-marched through the engine's grid in a box fitted to hold nearly all of the electron.
The fog depth is a display choice and is labelled as one. It sets how far into the cloud you see, not how much electron is there.

steps.title: From one state to another
body: With two states in the mix, the time-evolution view can walk from the first to the second. Every frame is a real, normalized state, never a blend of two pictures.
On the π-pulse path the density fades from one to the other, as a laser on resonance would drive it. In phase, the two interfere and the in-between frames lean to one side.
